page: Microsoft Azure D128s_v7 is a Dsv7-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, relying instead on Premium Storage compatibility for external disk attachments.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. This compute density is complemented by high memory bandwidth, reaching 9470.27 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 452.95 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and PassMark memory scores landing in the middle 50% average tier. However, the hardware excels in parallel processing tasks, as evidenced by top-tier results in Redis SET operations at 184.13 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 179.77 GB/sec.

The D128s_v7 offers high resource density for parallelized enterprise workloads, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for consolidation of multi-threaded applications without the overhead of managing multiple smaller instances. The primary tradeoffs include the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware, which limits its utility for direct hardware-accelerated deep learning training. However, the CPU features Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), enabling strong performance in CPU-based LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing. This server is suited for large-scale database operations, multi-threaded decompression, static web serving at scale, and high-throughput enterprise applications.
